locale.description: The code of this translation, exactly as the folder it lives in, such as de or pt_BR. Used to format times and numbers.

extDescription.message: Control your own browser with any AI agent you like: organise tabs and operate web pages over MCP.
extDescription.description: Extension description in the Chrome Web Store and on chrome://extensions. At most 132 characters. MCP is Model Context Protocol and stays in English.

actionTitle.message: Agent Browser Bridge: setup and status
actionTitle.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button before the extension has checked the connection. Agent Browser Bridge is the product name and is not translated.

actionTitleDisconnected.message: Agent Browser Bridge: no agent connected
actionTitleDisconnected.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button when no AI agent is connected.

actionTitleConnected.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button when an AI agent is connected but has not introduced itself.

actionTitleConnectedTo.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button. $1 is a comma-separated list of agent sessions, such as claude-code 2.1.3 in shop.

notificationReply.message: Click the Agent Browser Bridge toolbar button to reply
notificationReply.description: Small text under a desktop notification that shows a chat message from the agent.

optionsTitle.description: Browser tab title of the options page.

statusChecking.description: Shown while the extension checks whether an agent is connected.

statusLooking.description: Shown while the extension tries to reach the agent's local server.

welcomeLede.message: Let your AI agent organise your tabs and operate web pages.
welcomeLede.description: Subtitle of the setup page in Chrome.

welcomeLedeSafari.message: Let your AI agent find, open, move and close your Safari tabs.
welcomeLedeSafari.description: Subtitle of the setup page in Safari.

welcomeConnected.message: Connected: your agent can use the browser.
welcomeConnected.description: Connection status on the setup page when one agent session is connected.

welcomeConnectedMany_one.message: Connected: $1 agent session can use the browser.
welcomeConnectedMany_one.description: Connection status on the setup page. $1 is the number of connected agent sessions.

welcomeConnectedMany_other.message: Connected: $1 agent sessions can use the browser.
welcomeConnectedMany_other.description: Connection status on the setup page. $1 is the number of connected agent sessions.

welcomeDisconnected.message: Waiting for your agent. Set it up below, then start a session.
welcomeDisconnected.description: Connection status on the setup page when no agent is connected.

instanceNameLabel.description: Label of a text field where the user names this browser profile.

instanceNamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the browser profile name field.

welcomeInstanceNameHint.message: Agents use this name to tell your browsers and profiles apart, so you can ask for your Work browser. $1
welcomeInstanceNameHint.description: Help text under the browser profile name field on the setup page. $1 is replaced by the instance id, which may be empty. Translate Work the same way as in the placeholder.

optionsInstanceNameHint.message: Agents use this name to tell your browsers and profiles apart. $1
optionsInstanceNameHint.description: Help text under the browser profile name field in the options. $1 is replaced by the instance id, which may be empty.

instanceId.description: $1 is a short random identifier of this browser profile.

welcomeStepAdd.description: Heading of the first setup step.

welcomeStepAddHint.message: Your agent starts a small local server ($1) that this extension connects to. Pick your agent:
welcomeStepAddHint.description: $1 is a terminal command and is kept as is.

welcomeAgentSetupTitle.message: Let your agent set it up

welcomeAgentSetupBody.message: Paste this prompt into any agent that can run commands and edit its own settings, such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. It checks for Node.js, then adds the server.
welcomeAgentSetupBody.description: Card text. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Node.js are product names.

copyPrompt.description: Button that copies a prompt for the agent.

copy.description: Button that copies a command or configuration.

copied.description: Briefly shown on a copy button after copying.

welcomeClaudeCodeBody.description: Card text above a terminal command.

welcomeOpensAndConfirms.message: Opens the app and asks you to confirm.
welcomeOpensAndConfirms.description: Card text for the Cursor and VS Code install buttons.

welcomeAddTo.description: Button. $1 is an app name such as Cursor or VS Code.

welcomeClaudeDesktopBody.message: Download the extension, then open the file to install it. No Node.js needed.

welcomeDownloadFor.description: Button. $1 is an app name such as Claude Desktop.

welcomeOtherAgentsBody.message: Add this to the agent's MCP config, then restart it.
welcomeOtherAgentsBody.description: Card text above a JSON configuration snippet. MCP stays in English.

welcomeStepTry.description: Heading of the second setup step.

welcomeTryIntro.message: With Chrome open, ask your agent:

welcomeTryTabs.message: Organise my open tabs into groups by topic. Show me the plan first.
welcomeTryTabs.description: Example prompt the user can send to the agent.

welcomeTryPage.message: Open the Chrome release notes and summarise what changed in the latest version.
welcomeTryPage.description: Example prompt the user can send to the agent.

welcomeTryHint.message: The status above turns green once your agent's server is running. Changes made with $1 can be reverted by asking the agent to undo.
welcomeTryHint.description: $1 is a tool name and is kept as is.

welcomeTryIntroSafari.message: With Safari open, ask your agent:

welcomeTryDuplicatesSafari.message: Which tabs do I have open in Safari? Close the duplicates, but ask me first.
welcomeTryDuplicatesSafari.description: Example prompt the user can send to the agent.

welcomeTrySortSafari.message: Put my Safari tabs in order by site.
welcomeTrySortSafari.description: Example prompt the user can send to the agent.

welcomeTryHintSafari.message: The status above turns green once your agent's server is running. In Safari your agent can open, arrange and close windows, and open, navigate, switch, pin, mute, duplicate, move and close tabs. If tab titles and addresses are missing, give the extension website access in Safari under Settings > Extensions. Tab groups, history, bookmarks and page control are available in Chrome.
welcomeTryHintSafari.description: Use the names Safari shows for Settings and Extensions in this language.

welcomePrivacy.message: Your browsing data stays on your computer: the extension only talks to $1. Your agent can read tab titles and URLs, rearrange, group or close tabs, and read and act in web pages when you ask it to. Chrome shows a debugging banner while it works in a page. Tab titles, URLs and page contents are never sent anywhere else by this extension.

welcomePrivacySafari.message: Your browsing data stays on your computer: the extension only talks to $1. Your agent can read tab titles and URLs, and open, arrange or close windows and tabs when you ask it to. It cannot read or act in web pages in Safari. Tab titles and URLs are never sent anywhere else by this extension.

welcomeAnalytics.message: Share anonymous usage statistics (which features are used, extension version) to help improve the extension.

analyticsHint.message: Which features are used, whether they succeed, and the extension and agent versions. Never tab titles, URLs or page contents. $1
analyticsHint.description: Help text under the statistics checkbox. $1 is a link that reads Privacy policy.

analyticsUnavailable.message: This build does not collect usage statistics.
analyticsUnavailable.description: Shown in the options when the extension was built without analytics.

openSetup.description: Link from the options to the setup page.

optionsConnectedMany_one.description: Connection status in the options. $1 is the number of connected agent sessions.

optionsConnectedMany_other.description: Connection status in the options. $1 is the number of connected agent sessions.

agentStartingUp.description: Shown instead of the agent's name before it has introduced itself.

sessionInProject.description: $1 is an agent name and version, such as claude-code 2.1.3. $2 is the name of the project folder it works in.

sessionStarted.description: When an agent session started. $1 is a relative time such as 5 minutes ago.

sessionLastUsed_one.description: $1 is the number of tool calls, $2 a tool name such as chrome_tabs_list, $3 a relative time such as 5 minutes ago.

sessionLastUsed_other.description: $1 is the number of tool calls, $2 a tool name such as chrome_tabs_list, $3 a relative time such as 5 minutes ago.

sessionUnused.message: Has not used a browser yet
sessionUnused.description: Shown for an agent session that has not used any browser tool.

serverVersion.description: Tooltip. $1 is the version of the agent's local server.

instanceThisBrowser.description: Marks the browser profile the user is looking at. $1 is its name, such as Work (Chrome).

chatTitle.description: Title of the side panel where the user chats with the agent.

chatSetup.description: Link from the chat panel to the setup page.

chatConversation.description: Accessible name of the list that picks a conversation.

chatEmptyHeading.message: Talk to your agent from here
chatEmptyHeading.description: Heading shown in the chat panel when there is no conversation.

chatEmptyBody.message: Ask your agent to continue in the browser, or run its $1 prompt. Its messages appear here, and your replies go straight back to it.
chatEmptyBody.description: $1 is a prompt name and is kept as is.

chatEmptyHint.message: Each agent session gets its own conversation.
chatEmptyHint.description: Shown in the chat panel when there is no conversation.

chatInput.description: Placeholder of the chat message box.

chatRemove.description: Button that removes an ended conversation.

chatSend.description: Button that sends a chat message.

chatError.description: Generic error in the chat panel.

chatUnseen_one.description: Conversation in the picker with unread agent messages. $1 is the number of unread messages, $2 the conversation title.

chatUnseen_other.description: Conversation in the picker with unread agent messages. $1 is the number of unread messages, $2 the conversation title.

chatStatusWaiting.description: The agent is waiting for the user's message.

chatStatusWorkingTool.description: The agent is busy. $1 is a tool name such as chrome_tabs_list, $2 a relative time such as 5 minutes ago.

chatHintWaiting.message: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.
chatHintWaiting.description: Keyboard hint under the message box. Enter and Shift are key names.

chatHintWorking.message: The agent reads your message when it next checks the chat.
chatHintWorking.description: Hint under the message box while the agent is busy.

chatHintEnded.message: Ask the agent to continue in the browser to chat again.

chatReadByAgent.description: Under a message the user sent, after its time.

chatNotReadYet.description: Under a message the user sent, after its time.

chatEndedNotice.description: Notice in the conversation after the user ends it.

chatConversationGone.description: Error when sending to a removed conversation.

chatEndedError.message: This chat has ended. Ask the agent to continue in the browser to start it again.
chatEndedError.description: Error when sending to an ended conversation.

chatTooLong_one.message: Messages can be at most $1 character.
chatTooLong_one.description: Error. $1 is the maximum length of a chat message.

chatTooLong_other.message: Messages can be at most $1 characters.
chatTooLong_other.description: Error. $1 is the maximum length of a chat message.
